projectCategory: DSA Module 1.3: Stacks, Queues & Priority Buffers
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Fixed-Size Array Stack ADT with Overflow & Underflow Protection
projects.description: A Stack is a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) abstract data type where insertions (`push`) and deletions (`pop`) occur exclusively at the `top` index. In this project, you will build a Fixed-Size Array Stack in C. You will maintain a `top` integer index initialized to `-1`. When pushing, your program verifies that `top < MAX - 1` to prevent Stack Overflow; when popping, it verifies `top >= 0` to prevent Stack Underflow. You will implement `peek()` to inspect top values without removal.
projects.learningOutcome: LIFO Invariant, Stack Top Indexing & Overflow/Underflow Guarding
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Array Stack ADT ---
Pushed: 10
Pushed: 20
Pushed: 30
Popped: 30
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Initialize**: Set `top = -1`.
2. **Push**: Check `top < MAX - 1`, increment `top++`, assign `data[top] = val`.
3. **Pop**: Check `top >= 0`, return `data[top--]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push()` & `pop()`: Enforce LIFO stack rules with overflow/underflow checks.

projects.title: Dynamic Linked List Stack Implementation (Zero-Capacity Limit)
projects.description: Fixed-size array stacks fail when input size is unknown. A Linked List Stack allocates nodes dynamically on the heap, allowing the stack to grow dynamically without capacity limits until system RAM is exhausted. In this project, you will implement a Linked Stack in C. `push()` allocates a node and prepends it to `top` in O(1) time (`n->next = top; top = n;`), while `pop()` removes `top`, updates `top = top->next`, and frees heap memory.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Heap Stacks, O(1) Push/Pop via Head Relinking & Unlimited Buffer Growth
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Linked List Stack ---
Popped: 200
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Push**: Allocate node, `n->next = top`, set `top = n`.
2. **Pop**: Save `temp = top`, update `top = top->next`, `free(temp)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_link()` & `pop_link()`: Dynamic linked stack operations.

projects.title: String Reversal using Stack LIFO Principle
projects.description: Because a stack reverses the arrival sequence of elements (LIFO), pushing all characters of a string into a stack and popping them sequentially produces a perfectly reversed string! In this project, you will write a String Reversal Tool in C. Iterate through the string, pushing characters onto a character stack. Then pop characters one by one to overwrite the original string, demonstrating practical LIFO properties.
projects.learningOutcome: LIFO Sequence Inversion, Character Stack Buffers & In-Place String Modification
projects.exampleOutput:
--- String Reversal using Stack ---
Before: ANTIGRAVITY
After : YTIVARGINAT
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Push Pass**: Push each char `str[i]` to `stack[++top]`.
2. **Pop Pass**: Pop `stack[top--]` back into `str[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `reverse_string()`: Reverses string using character stack.

projects.title: Balanced Parentheses & Brackets Matcher
projects.description: Compilers and text editors use stacks to verify whether expression brackets (`()`, `{}`, `[]`) are correctly paired and nested. In this project, you will construct a Syntax Bracket Matcher in C. Scan the string: when encountering an opening bracket, push it onto the stack; when encountering a closing bracket, pop the top character and check if it matches the closing bracket type. If the stack is empty at the end, the string is balanced.
projects.learningOutcome: Syntax Parsing, Nested Bracket Matching & Stack Error State Handling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Balanced Parentheses Matcher ---
{[()]} → Balanced
{[(])} → Unbalanced
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Opening**: Push `(`, `{`, `[` onto stack.
2. **Closing**: Pop top and verify matching pair type.
3. **Validation**: Return true if stack is empty after scanning.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `is_balanced()`: Validates bracket pairing syntax.

projects.title: Standard Linear Queue ADT using Array
projects.description: A Queue is a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) data structure where items are inserted at `rear` (`enqueue`) and removed from `front` (`dequeue`). In this project, you will implement a Linear Array Queue in C with `front` and `rear` indices. You will observe how standard linear array queues suffer from false overflow when `rear` reaches capacity despite freed slots at `front`.
projects.learningOutcome: FIFO Invariant, Front/Rear Pointer Movement & Linear Queue Memory Drift
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Standard Linear Queue ---
Dequeued: 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Enqueue**: Increment `rear++`, `data[rear] = val`.
2. **Dequeue**: Return `data[front++]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `enqueue()` & `dequeue()`: Linear FIFO queue operations.

projects.title: Circular Queue ADT with Modulo Index Arithmetic
projects.description: Linear queues waste memory when items are dequeued. A Circular Queue wraps `rear` and `front` around to index 0 using modulo arithmetic: `idx = (idx + 1) % N`, turning memory into a continuous ring buffer. In this project, you will construct a Circular Queue in C that eliminates memory waste and recycles dequeued slots in O(1) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Circular Buffer Wraparound, Modulo Index Math & Memory Recycling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Circular Queue ADT ---
Dequeued: 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Circular Advance**: `rear = (rear + 1) % N`, `front = (front + 1) % N`.
2. **Full Condition**: `count == N`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `enqueue_c()` & `dequeue_c()`: Modulo circular queue implementation.

projects.title: Linked List Queue Implementation (Zero-Overflow Capacity)
projects.description: Like dynamic stacks, a Linked Queue dynamically grows node by node. Maintain `front` and `rear` pointers: `enqueue()` appends to `rear` in O(1) time, while `dequeue()` removes from `front` in O(1) time and frees node memory. In this project, you will build a dynamic Linked Queue in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic FIFO Queue, Dual Front/Rear Relinking & Zero Overflow Limit
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Linked List Queue ---
Dequeued: 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Enqueue**: Append to `rear->next`, update `rear`.
2. **Dequeue**: Remove `front`, update `front = front->next`, `free()` old front.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `enqueue_link()` & `dequeue_link()`: Dynamic linked queue operations.

projects.title: Double-Ended Queue (Deque) Array Implementation
projects.description: A Deque (Double-Ended Queue) allows insertion and deletion at BOTH ends (`push_front`, `push_back`, `pop_front`, `pop_back`). In this project, you will implement a Circular Array Deque in C, enabling O(1) operations at both boundaries.
projects.learningOutcome: Bi-Directional Queue Buffers, Deque Boundary Manipulation & Index Wraparound
projects.exampleText: Push Front 10, Push Back 20, Push Front 5
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Double-Ended Queue (Deque) ---
Front Element: 5, Rear Element: 20
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Front Operations**: `front = (front - 1 + N) % N`.
2. **Back Operations**: `rear = (rear + 1) % N`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_front()` & `push_back()`: Dual-ended deque operations.

projects.title: Reverse First K Elements of a Queue
projects.description: Given a queue and an integer K, reverse the order of the first K elements while keeping remaining elements in original relative order. In this project, you will implement K-Element Queue Reversal in C by dequeueing K elements onto an auxiliary stack and enqueueing them back.
projects.learningOutcome: Auxiliary Stack Data Transfer, Queue Subsegment Reversal & Data Stream Formatting
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Reverse First K Queue Elements ---
Before: [ 10 20 30 40 50 ]
After (K=3): [ 30 20 10 40 50 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Stack Dequeue**: Dequeue K items into stack.
2. **Stack Pop**: Pop stack items back into queue.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `reverse_first_k()`: Reverses first K queue items using stack buffer.

projects.title: Stack Min Tracker in O(1) Time Complexity
projects.description: Standard minimum searches take O(N) time. A Min Stack design tracks the minimum element in constant O(1) time using an auxiliary `min_stack` that records the running minimum at every push operation. In this project, you will build an O(1) Min Stack in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Auxiliary State Tracking, Running Minimum Invariants & O(1) Query Complexity
projects.exampleOutput:
--- O(1) Min Stack Engine ---
Current Min: 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Stack**: `main_stack` stores values, `min_stack` stores current min.
2. **Push Logic**: Push to `min_stack` if `val <= min_stack[top]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_min()` & `get_min()`: Maintains O(1) minimum query stack.

projects.title: Infix to Postfix Expression Conversion Engine (Shunting-Yard Algorithm)
projects.description: Computers evaluate math expressions in Postfix (Reverse Polish Notation) to eliminate parenthesis ambiguity. Dijkstra's Shunting-Yard Algorithm converts Infix (`a+b*c`) to Postfix (`abc*+`) using an operator stack and precedence rules. In this project, you will build a Shunting-Yard Converter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Shunting-Yard Algorithm, Operator Precedence Rules & Expression Parsing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Infix to Postfix Shunting-Yard ---
Infix  : a+b*(c^d-e)
Postfix: abcd^e-*+
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Operand**: Append directly to output.
2. **Operator**: Pop operators of higher/equal precedence to output, then push current operator.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `infix_to_postfix()`: Converts mathematical infix string to postfix RPN format.

projects.title: Postfix Expression Evaluator using Stack
projects.description: Evaluating a Postfix expression (`231*+9-`) is performed using an operand stack. Scan tokens from left to right: if operand, push to stack; if operator, pop two operands, perform operation, and push result back. In this project, you will build a Postfix Evaluator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Postfix RPN Evaluation, Stack Operand Operations & Compiler Expression Execution
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Postfix Expression Evaluator ---
Expression: 231*+9-
Evaluated Result = -4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Operand**: Push integer value to stack.
2. **Operator**: Pop `op2` and `op1`, compute `op1 op op2`, push result.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `evaluate_postfix()`: Computes mathematical value of postfix string.

projects.title: Implement Queue using Two Stacks
projects.description: A FIFO Queue can be simulated using two LIFO Stacks (`stack_in` and `stack_out`). `enqueue` pushes to `stack_in`. `dequeue` pops from `stack_out`; if `stack_out` is empty, pop all items from `stack_in` into `stack_out` (reversing LIFO twice to recreate FIFO!). In this project, you will build a Queue from Two Stacks in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Double LIFO Inversion to FIFO, Amortized O(1) Operations & Dual Stack State
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Queue using Two Stacks ---
Dequeued: 10
Dequeued: 20
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Push**: Always push to `stack_in`.
2. **Pop**: If `stack_out` empty, transfer all from `stack_in` to `stack_out`, then pop `stack_out`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `enqueue_q2s()` & `dequeue_q2s()`: Recreates FIFO queue behavior using 2 stacks.

projects.title: Implement Stack using Two Queues
projects.description: A LIFO Stack can be simulated using two FIFO Queues. When pushing a new element into `q2`, dequeue all elements from `q1` into `q2`, then swap `q1` and `q2`. In this project, you will build a Stack from Two Queues in C.
projects.learningOutcome: FIFO to LIFO State Transformation, Queue Swapping & Functional Data Structure Simulation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stack using Two Queues ---
Popped: 30
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Push**: Enqueue `val` to `q2`, move all `q1` items to `q2`, swap `q1` & `q2`.
2. **Pop**: Dequeue from `q1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_s2q()` & `pop_s2q()`: Simulates LIFO stack using 2 queues.

projects.title: Next Greater Element (NGE) using Monotonic Stack
projects.description: For each element in an array, find the first element to its right that is strictly greater. Brute force takes O(N^2) time. A Monotonic Decreasing Stack solves this in linear O(N) time! Iterate right-to-left, popping stack elements smaller than `arr[i]`. In this project, you will build a Monotonic NGE Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Stack Pattern, Linear O(N) Next Element Search & Stack Pruning
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Next Greater Element (Monotonic Stack) ---
Element  4 → NGE = 5
Element  5 → NGE = 25
Element  2 → NGE = 25
Element 25 → NGE = -1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Right-to-Left**: Loop `i` from `N-1` down to 0.
2. **Pop Smaller**: Pop stack while `stack[top] <= arr[i]`.
3. **Set NGE**: `NGE[i] = stack[top]`, then push `arr[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `next_greater_element()`: Computes NGE array using monotonic stack in O(N) time.

projects.title: Daily Temperatures / Next Warmer Day Index Finder
projects.description: Given an array of daily temperatures, find how many days you have to wait until a warmer temperature occurs. In this project, you will build a Monotonic Stack Temperature Index Finder in C that stores indices on a stack to find index differences in linear O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Index Stacks, Temperature Span Calculations & Range Processing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Daily Temperatures / Next Warmer Day ---
Days to wait: [ 1 1 4 2 1 1 0 0 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Index Stack**: Store index `i` on stack.
2. **Warmer Day Check**: Pop index `prev` while `temp[i] > temp[prev]`, set `ans[prev] = i - prev`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `daily_temperatures()`: Solves daily warmer temperature distance using monotonic index stack.

projects.title: Circular Tour / Gas Station Circuit Finder
projects.description: Suppose you have N gas stations on a circular route. Station `i` provides `gas[i]` fuel, and travel to next station costs `cost[i]` fuel. Find the starting gas station index from which you can travel full circuit once without running out of fuel. In this project, you will build a Gas Station Circuit Finder in C operating in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Greedy Fuel Accumulation, Circular Route Optimization & O(N) Single-Pass Circuit Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Gas Station Circular Circuit ---
Starting Gas Station Index = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Accumulate Surplus**: `curr_surplus += gas[i] - cost[i]`.
2. **Reset Point**: If `curr_surplus < 0`, reset `start = i + 1` and `curr_surplus = 0`.
3. **Global Check**: Valid if total gas >= total cost.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `can_complete_circuit()`: Finds starting gas station index for circular tour.

projects.title: First Non-Repeating Character in a Stream of Characters
projects.description: Given a continuous stream of characters, find the first non-repeating character after reading each character. In this project, you will build a Stream Processor in C combining a FIFO queue (storing order of characters) and a frequency array.
projects.learningOutcome: Stream Data Processing, Queue & Frequency Table Combination & Real-Time Filtering
projects.exampleOutput:
--- First Non-Repeating Character in Stream ---
Read 'a' → First Non-Repeating: 'a'
Read 'a' → First Non-Repeating: -1
Read 'b' → First Non-Repeating: 'b'
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Tally**: Increment `freq[char]++`, enqueue `char`.
2. **Queue Pruning**: Pop queue front while `freq[front] > 1`.
3. **Result**: `q.front` is first non-repeating character.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `first_non_repeating()`: Tracks real-time non-repeating character in data stream.

projects.title: Sort a Stack using a Temporary Auxiliary Stack
projects.description: Given an unsorted stack, sort its elements so that the smallest values are at the top using only ONE auxiliary stack (`tmp_stack`). In this project, you will build an In-Place Stack Sorting Engine in C operating in O(N^2) time.
projects.learningOutcome: In-Place Stack Insertion Sort, Auxiliary Stack Transfers & Sorting Invariants
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sort Stack using Auxiliary Stack ---
Sorted Stack (Top to Bottom): 3 23 31 34 92 98
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pop Target**: Pop `temp` from main stack.
2. **Prune Aux**: Pop `tmp_stack` back into main stack while `tmp_stack[top] > temp`.
3. **Push Temp**: Push `temp` into `tmp_stack`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sort_stack()`: Sorts stack elements using auxiliary stack.

projects.title: Sliding Window Maximum using Monotonic Double-Ended Queue
projects.description: Given an array and window size K, find maximum value in every sliding window of size K as it moves left to right. Brute force takes O(N * K) time. A Monotonic Deque stores indices of potential maximums in decreasing order, solving this in O(N) linear time! In this project, you will build a Monotonic Deque Sliding Window Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Deque Window Tracking, Linear O(N) Sliding Max & Queue Index Pruning
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sliding Window Maximum (Monotonic Deque) ---
Window Maxima (K=3): [ 3 3 5 5 6 7 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Out of Window**: Pop deque front if `deque[front] <= i - k`.
2. **Prune Smaller**: Pop deque rear while `arr[deque[rear]] <= arr[i]`.
3. **Window Max**: `arr[deque[front]]` is max for current window.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sliding_window_max()`: Computes sliding window maximums in linear O(N) time.

projects.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram (Monotonic Stack Boundary Engine)
projects.description: Given an array of heights representing a histogram, find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within the histogram bars. Brute force takes O(N^2) time. A Monotonic Increasing Stack finds left and right smaller boundaries for each bar in O(N) linear time! In this project, you will build a Monotonic Histogram Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Stack Histogram Analysis, Width/Height Boundary Calculations & O(N) Area Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Largest Rectangle in Histogram ---
Maximum Rectangular Area = 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Monotonic Stack**: Push bar indices maintaining increasing heights.
2. **Pop & Calculate**: When encountering smaller height `h`, pop `stack` and compute `area = height * (i - stack[top] - 1)`.
3. **Max Area**: Track global maximum area.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `largest_rectangle_area()`: Calculates maximum histogram rectangle in O(N) time.

projects.title: Maximal Binary Matrix Rectangle Finder (2D Monotonic Stack)
projects.description: Given a 2D binary matrix filled with 0s and 1s, find the largest rectangle containing only 1s and return its area. By converting each matrix row into a histogram of consecutive 1s and running 1D Largest Rectangle in Histogram for each row, this problem is solved in O(R * C) time! In this project, you will build a 2D Maximal Matrix Rectangle Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Grid Matrix to Histogram Reduction, Monotonic Stack Integration & O(R*C) Matrix Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximal Rectangle in Binary Matrix ---
Maximal Rectangle Area = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Row Histograms**: Accumulate height of consecutive 1s for each column.
2. **Run Histogram Area**: Execute 1D Largest Histogram Area on accumulated height array for each row.
3. **Global Max**: Return max area found across all rows.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `maximal_rectangle()`: Computes largest binary matrix rectangle in O(R * C) time.

projects.title: Circular Buffer Ring (Lock-Free Producer-Consumer Thread Communication)
projects.description: In operating systems, real-time audio streams, and multi-threaded systems, a Lock-Free Ring Buffer passes data between a Producer thread and a Consumer thread without mutex locks. Maintain `head` and `tail` atomic/volatile indices. In this project, you will build a Lock-Free Circular Ring Buffer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lock-Free Data Structures, Atomic Head/Tail Ring Buffers & Thread Communications
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lock-Free Circular Ring Buffer ---
Popped from Ring: 100
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Head/Tail Volatile**: `head` moved by Producer, `tail` moved by Consumer.
2. **Lock-Free Check**: `(head + 1) % N == tail` means full; `head == tail` means empty.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ring_push()` & `ring_pop()`: Implements lock-free circular ring buffer.

projects.title: Expression Tree Construction & Postorder Evaluation Engine
projects.description: Compilers convert Postfix expressions into binary Expression Trees where internal nodes are operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) and leaf nodes are operands. Postorder traversal evaluates the tree. In this project, you will build an Expression Tree Builder and Evaluator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Expression Tree Data Structures, Postfix Tree Building & Recursive Evaluation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Expression Tree Construction & Evaluation ---
Postfix: 53+82/*
Tree Evaluated Result = 32
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Build Tree**: Scan postfix; operands pushed to stack as leaf nodes; operators pop 2 subtrees and push operator node.
2. **Evaluate Tree**: Recursively evaluate left and right subtrees and compute operator.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_expression_tree()` & `eval_tree()`: Builds and evaluates binary expression tree.

projects.title: Min-Max Stack & Queue (O(1) Time Min, Max, Push, Pop Engine)
projects.description: Build an advanced Stack data structure that supports `push()`, `pop()`, `get_min()`, AND `get_max()` all in O(1) constant time complexity! Maintain parallel running minimum and running maximum stacks alongside main value stack. In this project, you will build a Min-Max Stack in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Running Invariant Tracking, O(1) Min/Max Query Design & Multi-Stack Architecture
projects.exampleOutput:
--- O(1) Min-Max Stack Engine ---
Current Min = 5, Current Max = 40
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Triple Stack Invariant**: `val_stack`, `min_stack`, `max_stack` updated simultaneously.
2. **State Updates**: `min_stack[top] = min(val, min_stack[top-1])`, `max_stack[top] = max(val, max_stack[top-1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_minmax()`, `get_min()`, `get_max()`: Performs O(1) min and max stack tracking.
